source_locations: Proposition 3.39 Step 2, PDF pp22–23; exact embedding assertion p23
issues.counterexample: Take A'=Z_p<t>, A=Z_p<t,t^-1>, R=A and M=0. These are reduced formal affinoids with Spf A the formal principal open in Spf A', and A'=O^+(T'_Qp). The series z=sum_(n>=1)p^n t^(-n^2) is in A. For any nonzero g=sum g_jt^j in A', choose a=min v_p(g_j), v_p(g_d)=a. For 2n>d+1 the coefficient of t^(d-n^2) in gz equals p^n g_d modulo p^(a+n+1), hence is nonzero. Thus gz has infinitely many negative exponents and cannot be in A'. Therefore z notin Frac(A'), and Spec A→Spec A' has a strict generic residue-field extension, impossible for an immersion.

source_locations: Proposition2.22 proof Step2 PDF p9; Example2.3 p5 and Definition2.14 pp6–7
issues.counterexample: For A=Q_p<T,T^-1>^dagger, d:A→A dT has kernel Q_p, exact forms have residue zero, and dT/T has residue one. Residue-zero forms have primitives after shrinking by exponential-over-polynomial coefficient control. Hence H0=Q_p,H1=Q_p and dR(Torus)=1⊕1[-1], as LBV Cor4.37(6) confirms.
issues.core_impact: The false unreduced torus equality is the actual premise for extending the effective realization through Tate stabilization in Prop2.22, an essential input to the main realization chain. With e:1→M and p:M→1, pe=id, contravariance gives R(Tred)=fib(R(e)). The printed R(M)=1 over Spa Qp would make the split epimorphism R(e) an isomorphism and the Tate image zero, not tensor-invertible.
issues.counterevidence: The correct two-summand torus realization gives R(Tred)=1[-1], which is invertible and repairs this stabilization step. Neither the intended stabilized realization nor the final Berthelot theorem is disproved; repairability does not downgrade an actual core proof defect.
issues.repair_boundary: Replace the unreduced unit equality by the two-summand computation, use the section and augmentation to identify the reduced Tate image, and then invoke the localization universal property. This supplies this step, not the unverified remainder of the comparison.

source_locations: Remark2.27 and Definition2.25 PDF p10; dagger map definition p5; actual Cor2.28 proof p11
issues.counterexample: The allowed analytic map from completed unit disc into P1_Qp given by F(T)=sum p^nT^(n!) has exact convergence radius1. Any dagger morphism to the alleged terminal object would extend it meromorphically to a larger closed disc. The inverse image of infinity is a proper zero-dimensional closed analytic subset of a one-dimensional affinoid, hence finite. No poles lie on the unit disc, so some radius>1 is pole-free and gives an impossible analytic extension.

checks.independent_check: For z=sum p^n t^-n^2 and nonzero g=sum g_jt^j, choose minimal coefficient valuation a attained at d. For sufficiently large n with 2n>d+1, every m<n contribution to exponent d-n^2 vanishes, the m=n term has valuation a+n, and all m>n terms have larger valuation. Thus gz has arbitrarily negative nonzero coefficients and z is not in Frac(A'). The generic residue fields differ, which an immersion cannot do.
